newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy unions threaten to widen metalworkers strike.
newsitem.headline: Italy unions threaten to widen metalworkers strike.

text.p: Workers in the Italian industrial and transport sectors will stage a four-hour strike by the end of November if the engineering and metalworkers dispute is not resolved, the head of one of Italy's big three unions said.
Italy's 1.5 million engineering and metalworkers announced last week they would hold an eight-hour stoppage on November 15 as part of their increasingly bitter fight with employers for higher wages.

"If between now and November 15 the negotiations aren't resolved, towards the end of (next) month there will be a four hour strike in the industrial and transport sectors," Sergio D'Antoni, leader of the Cisl union, told reporters. Some 6.8 million workers would be involved in the threatened action.

Talks between unions and management over the new metal workers' contracts broke down last month and no fresh contacts between the two sides are planned. Metalworkers and engineers have already held one eight-hour strike in September.

The dispute has become a battle over how to interpret a landmark 1993 labour pact, which scrapped automatic index- linking of salaries on condition that management would make up any shortfall in wages if inflation ran above target.

However the wording of the accord was deliberately vague. Unions have interpreted it to mean that all the inflation overshoot should be covered. Employers argue that only a part of lost earnings need be made up.
